taxonomic_note: Species-level learner concept, distinct from the other Elymus species in this batch. Hybrids and infraspecific variants can blur characters; use an intact mature spikelet and do not force a hybrid/intermediate into either species.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: inspect a mature, intact seed spike. Canada wildrye typically arches or nods with conspicuously long spreading/curved lemma awns. At a rachis node, check paired or sometimes three spikelets, then the narrow glumes with comparatively straight, V-like bases (not the strongly bowed, bony U-like bases typical of E. virginicus).

best_field_traits: Tufted cool-season perennial grass with jointed culms and leaf auricles.
Terminal unbranched spike often arching/nodding at maturity; usually 2–3 spikelets per rachis node.
Lemma awns usually long (often 15–40 mm), spreading or curving outward, giving a shaggy look.
Glumes relatively narrow; bases commonly straight or only slightly hardened, not distinctly U-bowed.
Leaf blades may be relatively broad; leaf width alone is not reliable.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Versus E. virginicus: usually a more nodding, open/shaggy mature spike, longer divergent awns and glumes with straighter V-like bases. E. virginicus generally retains an erect tighter spike, shorter straighter awns and hardened outward-bowed U-like glume bases. Hybrids and variable forms occur; require several intact spikelets.
